## Learning Objective

Interpret the coefficients when the outcome has been logged.


## Lesson

### Math

Suppose we change our model to
$$
\log_a Y_i|X_i \sim N\left(\beta_0 + \beta_1 X_i,\sigma^2\right) \text{.}
$$
How do we interpret the coefficients then?

$\beta_0$ is the expected value of the log of the outcome
when $X_i = 0$:
$$
E\left(\log_a Y_i\middle|X_i = 0\right) = \beta_0 \text{.}
$$

::: {.callout-caution collapse="true"}
## Caution: Math

Define $Z_i = \log_a Y_i$.
Then 
$$
Z_i|X_i \sim N\left(\beta_0 + \beta_1 X_i,\sigma^2\right)
$$
and
$$
f(z|x) = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi\sigma^2}} \exp\left(-\frac{\left(z - \beta_0 - \beta_1 x\right)^2}{2\sigma^2}\right) \text{.}
$$
Further,
$$
Y_i = a^{Z_i}
$$
and
$$
\begin{align*}
E\left(Y_i\middle|X_i = x\right) &= E\left(a^{Z_i}\middle|X_i = x\right) \\
&= \int_{-\infty}^\infty a^z f(z|x)\,dz \\
&= \int_{-\infty}^\infty a^z \frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi\sigma^2}} \exp\left(-\frac{\left(z - \beta_0 - \beta_1 x\right)^2}{2\sigma^2}\right) \,dz \\
\end{align*}
$$

If $\log_a Y_i|X_i \sim N\left(\beta_0 + \beta_1 X_i,\sigma^2\right)$
then
$$
\begin{align*}
E\left(Y_i\middle|X_i\right) &=
\end{align*}
$$

:::

### Forest Fire Example

Each observation is a forest fire in Montesinho Park (Portugal)
between January 2000 and December 2003
where at least 0.01 hectare (100 square meters) was burned.
In the figure below,
I've plotted $\log_{10}(\text{area burned})$ as a function of the outside
temperature.
```{r}
d <- Lock5Data::ForestFires
d$Area_No_0 <- d$Area
d$Area_No_0[d$Area_No_0 == 0] <- NA
d$Log10_Area_No_0 <- log10(d$Area_No_0)
plot(x = d$Temp,
     y = d$Log10_Area_No_0,
     xlab = "Outside Temperature (degrees Celsius)",
     ylab = "Log10(Total Burned Area) (log hectares)")
mod_01 <- lm(formula = Log10_Area_No_0 ~ Temp,
             data = d)
plot(x = mod_01$model$Temp,
     y = mod_01$residuals,
     xlab = "Outside Temperature (degrees Celsius)",
     ylab = "Residuals")
abline(h = 0,
       col = "red")
```
